latest_release.name: open-compute 0.4.0
latest_release.body:
Open Compute 0.4.0 adds Container execution and snapshot paths for single-machine deployments.
Publication requires every revision-bound release qualification job to pass.

## What's new

- The implementation adds an operator-owned Container Broker and immutable Container targets.
  Code-only deployment keeps the current execution.
  Image or resource deployment creates a new target and retires the previous execution.
- Durable Object containers gain process lifecycle, HTTP and WebSocket transport, exec streams, named images, inactivity policy and snapshot code paths.
  The local product cases exercise these paths with real workerd, Docker and SQLite.
- Snapshot capture retains filesystem data and excludes volatile `/run` data.
  Snapshot restore creates a new execution from the retained image.
  Artifact ownership and bounded cleanup remain explicit.
- The Container registry accepts ordered OCI manifests that reference a layer more than once.
  Every descriptor retains its digest and size checks; each blob enters the admission set once.

## Workerd

The candidate uses `v1.20260930.0-open-compute-r24.9de631551` at `9de631551791218aed0c4cd570163cece3c00590`.
The previous release used `v1.20260930.0-open-compute-r4.e98a3e843` at `e98a3e8433979356047a202d3e0d1b0e2e2c4b8c`.
Both binaries print `workerd 2026-09-30`.
The pin and lock digest identify the runtime change.

Container callbacks retain the public Durable Object and Service binding policy checks during HTTP and WebSocket streams.
Lease fences prevent a callback from completing a replacement execution.
Automatic monitor calls do not extend the tenant's inactivity timer.
Container snapshots enter a fresh event under the original owner before the platform captures the container image.
Private Container actors expose the configured immutable image map.
Directory snapshot inputs pass through the original owner event and its existing binding checks.
The Broker uses private Container protocol v4 to restore captured directories before the main process starts.
The event loop polls Tokio readiness while KJ remains busy, so large uploads do not monopolize runtime I/O.
The HTTP client closes HTTP/1.0 connections by default and retains explicit keep-alive behavior.
The owning regression checks reuse before EOF arrives, rather than waiting for connection closure.

The previous source gitlink was `fdcb8c97f0b9f75f610b66e418d5175b9188ddad`.
That gitlink includes a publication-path repair after the formal R4 pin.
The current `third_party/workerd` gitlink is `9de631551791218aed0c4cd570163cece3c00590`.
The formal binary source uses that same revision.
The following table contains all 29 commits between those source gitlinks.
Commit subjects retain their original text.

| [8903b3504393](https://github.com/elliothux/workerd/commit/8903b35043930eb4a5e75a56e918d8c1982eb14b) | Drop managed application packet capture capability                            |
| [fb1a903f1e89](https://github.com/elliothux/workerd/commit/fb1a903f1e89c183f5612e2e6c1003a3fa1da07a) | Serialize Container lease admission and confirm normal process exit           |
